feedback.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=0\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
feedback.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+t \\ 2-t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
